nodes.text: 'Is it always better to tell the truth, or is it sometimes best to lie? Write an essay, blah blah blah. Use personal, literary, and historical examples to defend your argument.'

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Stupid essay... Okay, twenty minutes to write this sucker, and I'm not `gaining` time!
nodes.text_bbcode: Stupid essay... Okay, twenty minutes to write this sucker, and I'm not [color=#3b78e2][i]gaining[/i][/color] time!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: `I` think it's always best to tell the truth because lies can harm! So what's a good `personal` example to back that up?
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]I[/i][/color] think it's always best to tell the truth because lies can harm! So what's a good [color=#3b78e2][i]personal[/i][/color] example to back that up?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'll write about the time...

options.label: My ex-boyfriend Colt cheated on me.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: A football executive?

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I don't know much about football I'm afraid. But that `seems` impressive.
nodes.text_bbcode: I don't know much about football I'm afraid. But that [color=#3b78e2][i]seems[/i][/color] impressive.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: I'm not familiar with the sport myself. Polo is my forte. What does he do exactly? Work with professionals?
Owen thinks of the high school guys from his old school.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Potential professionals.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Very interesting.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: He seems to think so.
Paige leans over and whispers.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: An executive? You made that up. He's just a coach, isn't he?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I don't know what you're talking about.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Uh-huh.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: So... He enjoys football? That's it?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: So he does nothing, is what you're saying.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh, no, I didn't mean it that way. He does `something`. It's just always related to football.
nodes.text_bbcode: Uh, no, I didn't mean it that way. He does [color=#e23b3b][i]something[/i][/color]. It's just always related to football.

nodes.text: Owen stumbles as his mind races.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh, he's a football fan?

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Now Owen, what does your father do?
Owen thinks of his dad, who's still coaching football at the local high school far away from here.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Somehow I don't think they're going to be that impressed with a high school football coach...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: He's a...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Or at least that's what I hear.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: You're familiar with the sport?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Um, familiar enough. It's horse training, isn't it?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Yes. It is `training.` Some people call dressage 'horse ballet', but I don't like that term. Dressage is a gentleman's sport, not some sort of gaudy, cheap entertainment.
nodes.text_bbcode: Yes. It is [color=#e23b3b][i]training.[/i][/color] Some people call dressage 'horse ballet', but I don't like that term. Dressage is a gentleman's sport, not some sort of gaudy, cheap entertainment.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I'd hardly lump 'ballet' into the 'gaudy, cheap entertainment' category.
She and Paige laugh, and Owen relaxes.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Those Oldenburg horses are good at, uh, fromage? Right? The sport?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Surely you jest. I can't possibly believe that you've mixed up `dressage,` one of the greatest sports in the gentlemanly world with... With a basic French food!
nodes.text_bbcode: Surely you jest. I can't possibly believe that you've mixed up [color=#e23b3b][i]dressage,[/i][/color] one of the greatest sports in the gentlemanly world with... With a basic French food!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, actually, that's probably more believable than me knowing what `dressage` is.
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, actually, that's probably more believable than me knowing what [color=#e23b3b][i]dressage[/i][/color] is.

nodes.text: Paige makes an exasperated sound. Margot clears her throat.
Owen's brain suddenly seizes up, and he blanks!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Uh...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Yes?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Say something French!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Fromage?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Bah! You're just as tasteless as the rest of them.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Arabians aren't the best horse?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: No! Of course not! It is the noble Oldenburg that is the greatest steed! You are as ignorant as you are unfashionable.
Paige winces.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Er, so... Oldenburgs! They're quite good for...
Tad coughs into his napkin, stunned by Owen's comment. Paige smiles smugly.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Why, that's the breed of horse I find the most noble!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yes, they're quite good for...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Well, speak up. Which breed do you like the best?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Arabian?
Inside the restaurant, Owen and Paige walk up to the maitre d'.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I have a reservation for two.
The maitre d' checks the reservations booklet. His smile widens when he sees her name.

nodes.speaker: Maitre D'
nodes.text: Mademoiselle Paige. It is a pleasure to have you at The Prime Cut. Are you still waiting for your guest?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm right here.

nodes.speaker: Maitre D'
nodes.text: You? You are `her` guest?
nodes.text_bbcode: You? You are [color=#e23b3b][i]her[/i][/color] guest?

nodes.text: He eyes Owen's t-shirt with undisguised distaste.

nodes.speaker: Maitre D'
nodes.text: I am sorry, but we have certain standards to maintain. Your guest is underdressed for our formal dining room.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Can't you dress well for anything?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You could try warning me for once.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Want to leave?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Not particularly.
Paige sighs and takes the maitre d' aside.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Is there any way that I could `convince` you to let my guest in? Perhaps you have something `suitable` for him to don while we dine?
nodes.text_bbcode: Is there any way that I could [color=#3b78e2][i]convince[/i][/color] you to let my guest in? Perhaps you have something [color=#3b78e2][i]suitable[/i][/color] for him to don while we dine?

nodes.text: She surreptitiously slips a couple bills in his hand when she shakes it. The maitre d' smiles.

nodes.speaker: Maitre D'
nodes.text: Of course, we cannot always expect our guests to arrive in impeccable condition. Come, come with me!
The maitre d' drags Owen away.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Whoa, whoa, what's going on?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You need the proper attire. He's getting it for you. Go with him, and I'll see you in the dining room!
A few minutes later, Owen walks into the dining room wearing an old tuxedo jacket. With his dark black jeans, his outfit passes for formal.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Not too bad!
He spots Paige in the back corner of the restaurant at a table partially obscured by a red curtain. When Paige sees him, she shakes her head at him and winces.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I wonder what's wrong with her?
Ignoring her head-shaking, he walks towards her, stops at the table...
And realizes she is not alone.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh, uh, hi!
Paige's mother Margot and her stepfather Tad glare condescendingly at Owen.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: It's you!

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: `This` is your gentleman suitor, Paige?
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]This[/i][/color] is your gentleman suitor, Paige?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: `Yes.`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]Yes.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: The last time we talked, you told us you wanted to be rid of him!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: If I find out you've lied about seeing him, young lady, your next boarding school will be in Switzerland!
Owen opens his mouth to protest, but Paige railroads over him.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I didn't lie to you! I `was` through with him! It's just that, in the last few weeks, he's proven to me that he's not the peasant he used to be.
nodes.text_bbcode: I didn't lie to you! I [color=#3b78e2][i]was[/i][/color] through with him! It's just that, in the last few weeks, he's proven to me that he's not the peasant he used to be.

nodes.text: Margot and Tad exchange a look.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: That remains to be seen. Sit down, boy.
Reluctantly, Owen takes the empty seat next to Paige. She squeezes his hand underneath the table.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: What? Are you sure about this, Margot, my silver dollar?

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: No. But Paige has been doing so well at Monarch Prep. I suppose I should give this `boy` a chance if she seems to think he deserves one.
nodes.text_bbcode: No. But Paige has been doing so well at Monarch Prep. I suppose I should give this [color=#3b78e2][i]boy[/i][/color] a chance if she seems to think he deserves one.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Fine. But one embarrassing mistake, and we are leaving. I can't be seen with a hooligan in `that` outfit. I have distinguished friends who frequent this establishment.
nodes.text_bbcode: Fine. But one embarrassing mistake, and we are leaving. I can't be seen with a hooligan in [color=#e23b3b][i]that[/i][/color] outfit. I have distinguished friends who frequent this establishment.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I'm sure it won't be a problem. Right?!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Er, no!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Keep it cool!
Silence falls on their table. Paige glares at her plate, and Margot and Tad keep studying Owen.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, I don't want them to strike first...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So, Tad, Paige mentioned you were interested in horses. I've always thought that the best breed of horse was the...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You mean 'steal a golf cart'?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, I have every intention of giving it back. Just `after` we drive it away from the clubhouse for a while. Come on!
nodes.text_bbcode: Hey, I have every intention of giving it back. Just [color=#e23b3b][i]after[/i][/color] we drive it away from the clubhouse for a while. Come on!

nodes.text: They sneak around the carts until Owen finds one with the key in the ignition. They climb in and drive the cart down onto the plush greenery of the golf course.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Go, go, go!
Owen floors the gas pedal on the cart.
It doesn't go any faster.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: We're at max, I guess.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I could run faster than this.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: And take out all the romance? Look at the trees going slowly by! Smell the trimmed grass! Listen to the gentle hum of this golf cart's poor engine!
Paige only laughs as the wind catches her hair. With the clubhouse out of sight, Owen drives the cart around a bend and parks it in a small clearing.
Setting down clean golf towels, they lie on the grass and look up at the stars.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, remember our Valentine's date? We were in a park just like this.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Were we? I forgot.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You're the worst.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Oh wait, I remember. I did this.
Paige leans over and kisses him.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You did not.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Just shut up already.
He kisses her back.
Later, they drive the cart back to the clubhouse and head to the front desk of the restaurant.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What? You really want to do that?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Sure! Why not?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You are so dense.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Nothing. Let's go hit something.
Owen takes a bucket of golf balls and grabs a club from a golf bag on the side of the driving range.
He takes the club in both hands and swings. Paige snorts with laughter.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well, you're obviously a `football` player.
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, you're obviously a [color=#3b78e2][i]football[/i][/color] player.

nodes.text: Paige comes over, positions herself behind him, and helps him hold the club correctly.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: So you bring it back like so...
She shows him how to draw the club back.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: ...And then you swing down at the ball. Easy.
She steps back and watches him take a swing.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Not like that. Geez. It's so easy, a six-year-old could do it.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Thanks, Coach. Your words are inspiring as always.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Yeah, they are. Now try hitting it with an actual golf ball. Maybe if you have a target, you'll actually swing right.
Owen rolls his eyes but does as she says.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay, now watch this!
Owen swings down at the ball with all his might...
And sends the ball high! It hits a post in the driving range and ricochets into the parking lot! They hear the ominous sound of glass breaking!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh no...
Frantically, Paige and Owen run out into the parking lot and start checking cars for broken windows.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: The good news is that we didn't break the window of some fancy pants rich-mobile...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: The bad news is we may have a chilly ride home.
Owen points to the driver side window of his truck. Cracks spiral out from a golf ball-sized hole. He sighs.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well, at least it wasn't someone else's car.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Just forget about it, okay?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Let's just have a good time.
Owen lets her lead him inside the clubhouse.
They run into the clubhouse and head for the front desk of the restaurant.
Owen turns into a driveway that opens up onto a fancy country club!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: ...This is it!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I see it, but I can't believe I'm at a golf course. Where have you taken us?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: The Crystal Uplands Country Club. They have a steakhouse with `real` steak... Not the scraps you're used to. I made us dinner reservations for 7 p.m.!
nodes.text_bbcode: The Crystal Uplands Country Club. They have a steakhouse with [color=#3b78e2][i]real[/i][/color] steak... Not the scraps you're used to. I made us dinner reservations for 7 p.m.!

nodes.text: Owen checks the time on his phone.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Why'd you make me get you so early? We have forty-five minutes until the reservation.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I didn't know you were going to drive us here so fast.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Besides, now we can hang out. Just us. `Off campus.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Besides, now we can hang out. Just us. [color=#3b78e2][i]Off campus.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What do you want to do?
Paige looks at the clubhouse windows where patrons of the restaurant can see everything on the terrace that they're standing on.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Find someplace... Quiet.
Owen eyes the golf carts near them on the left and the driving range just a few hundred yards away on the right.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Why don't we...

options.label: Hit balls on the driving range?

nodes.text: Owen reaches over to Paige's stomach and tickles her!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: `Gah!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]Gah![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What are you doing?!
Paige starts flailing her arms around to get out of range.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Ahhhh!
She whacks Owen's arm so hard that the truck swerves just a little bit off the road onto the dirt pullout on the side.
Owen tightens his grip on the steering wheel and keeps the truck on the pavement.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Watch it, handsy!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I should be the one complaining! You're swatting at me!
After a moment of flustered silence, Paige glares at Owen.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I. Don't. Like. Being. Tickled.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay, okay, I get it. I was trying to... Support you.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: By getting us into an accident?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It was not my best plan!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: But it did distract you, didn't it?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I'm not sure I need to be `distracted.`
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm not sure I need to be [color=#3b78e2][i]distracted.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Even though maybe you were kind of cute enough to try.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Whoa, hey, turn right here!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So let me get this straight. Your week was really hard because you had to talk about horses, drink inferior coffee, and use your secondary computer?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Do you have to say it like it's the lamest thing in the world?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh, yeah!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Because it pretty much is. You know, there are people who worry about the shirt on their back.
Paige snorts with derision and then laughs.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: The shirt on their back? You mean, like you? Because that shirt you're wearing is just a tragedy.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hmph. See if I try to support you and your high-class rich people problems.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: If this is your idea of supporting me, I'd hate to see what `not` supporting me is like.
nodes.text_bbcode: If this is your idea of supporting me, I'd hate to see what [color=#3b78e2][i]not[/i][/color] supporting me is like.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hey, this is us! Make a right up here!
You are now playing as Owen.
That evening, Owen picks up Paige just outside the gates of Monarch Prep. Paige climbs in, giving the truck a quick once-over.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Where'd you get this rust bucket? A 1950s junkyard?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm sorry, but we can't all have gold limos from the future with plush interior seating.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You say that like it's an insult.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It is when you consider that I said gold, not platinum.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Touche, Owen.
He leans over and kisses her.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You seem happy. You've only insulted me once. What's the occasion?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hey, this is my first night out of Monarch Prep since the Debutante Dance! Do you know how boring it is on campus?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Paige, your school has an on-campus mall. How bad can it be?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Exactly. `One` mall. Yawn!
nodes.text_bbcode: Exactly. [color=#3b78e2][i]One[/i][/color] mall. Yawn!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It always shocks me to think that we're somehow dating.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Shut up. You love it. You're obviously getting the better deal here.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh-huh. Where to, Your Majesty?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Take a right at the gate, and we're going to follow the winding path up the hill.
Owen puts his truck into gear and starts off.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: How are you?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Honestly, I could totally be better. It's been an awful week.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What happened?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: First, my parents are in town, so that means I have to put up with visits from Margot and Tad.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Tad keeps going on and on about horses! I don't care that an Oldenburg is better than an Arabian in dressage!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh, were any of the words you just said actual words?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Dressage is a kind of horse training. But anyway, that's not the only problem. The little cafe off campus just closed! Where else am I going to get my medio, non-fat, no foam, extra chocolate espresso with wildflower honey stick?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Again. Perfectly normal words.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: But the worst part is that my laptop mini totally crashed while I was going to classes, so I had to take my backup, which is half a pound heavier! So annoying.
She pouts, and Owen sighs.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Even though her problems are... Weird... That doesn't mean I can't cheer her up.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, I'm sorry to hear that.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I don't need your pity. Especially if it's sarcastic.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay, now what?
$ZOE can feel tears welling up in her eyes, but they're soon replaced with anger.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: You can't do this to me! Why did you kick me off?
The other cheerleaders on the team stop what they're doing to watch.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: You know why, $ZOE! You were blowing off too many practices!
Missy gasps.

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: You were?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Yeah, because I got a little busy.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: A `little` busy? You hardly ever showed up! The team needed you, and you weren't there!
nodes.text_bbcode: A [color=#3b78e2][i]little[/i][/color] busy? You hardly ever showed up! The team needed you, and you weren't there!

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: `You` could at least have had the decency to quit first!
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]You[/i][/color] could at least have had the decency to quit first!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Maria...

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: We're done talking. I've already started looking for your replacement.
Maria storms off, and Missy comes to confront $ZOE.

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: Was that all true?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Yeah. But I did `care` about the team. I just had my hands full.
nodes.text_bbcode: Yeah. But I did [color=#3b78e2][i]care[/i][/color] about the team. I just had my hands full.

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: But back to cheerleading for a second... So tell me a bit more. How often do you practice?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Up to three times a week. We even practice on Fridays.

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: But today is Friday.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Yeah, I had to miss today's practice for this interview--

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: Oh no!

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: $ZOE, you don't have to do that on my account! Cheerleading is very important, and I'd hate for you to miss out on practice.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: No, it's okay. Practice is pretty short today...

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: All the more reason that it's perfect for you to go!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: But our interview--

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: It's fine! I'll watch from the sidelines. You know, this is totally exciting! I haven't seen a high school cheerleading team since I was in high school!

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: It'll be so much fun!
They walk towards the football field, while Missy chatters on.

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: My major was in cheerleading, you know.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Oh! I didn't know... Uh, that you could study that. At Kingston. Aren't they known for having an amazing science program?

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: Well, yeah! That's why I went! For the `science` of cheerleading!
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, yeah! That's why I went! For the [color=#3b78e2][i]science[/i][/color] of cheerleading!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Really. The science of `cheerleading.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Really. The science of [color=#3b78e2][i]cheerleading.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: They turn a corner and walk onto the field where they see Jill run, leap, and flip around twice!

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: You see that there? She could have made it a third time if she ran just a touch faster right before the jump. Her mass times her acceleration isn't generating enough force for her turn.
$ZOE gapes at Missy Perkins, who grins.

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: Newton's Second Law! It never hurts to remember that during tumbling.
Missy and $ZOE walk up to Maria.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Hey, Maria...

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: What are you doing here?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Uh, well, I had an interview scheduled for Kingston, so I skipped practice today, but it turns out Missy here wants to watch me practice.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Well, good luck with that. Unfortunately, this practice is for cheerleaders who haven't been kicked off the squad.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Missy
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: But... But...
